observations.scope: Native RegisterScalableTarget initial registration and existing suspension updates for one owned zero-task ECS service, bounds 0/0, preexisting global linked roles.
conclusions: All 16 RegisterScalableTarget calls returned HTTP 200, including missing both ECS actions and explicit denies of each action. Each initial call created a target; each existing call changed suspension flags, observed immediately and after three seconds.

ECS IAM checks do occur in forwarded original-caller DescribeServices and UpdateService calls. CloudTrail reports AccessDenied for missing or explicitly denied actions, yet these downstream denials did not become RegisterScalableTarget denials in this bounded scenario.
The caller with neither ECS action was denied both forwarded ECS operations; Application Auto Scaling still registered and changed the target while its linked role successfully described the service.

Allowed caller UpdateService admission requests recorded internal desiredCount:-1 and InvalidParameterException. No public ECS desiredCount:-1 request was sent, and this is not evidence that public ECS UpdateService accepts -1.

ViaAWSService=true and CalledVia containing application-autoscaling.amazonaws.com each allowed forwarded DescribeServices and reached internal UpdateService InvalidParameterException, while direct ECS calls using the same conditional role sessions returned AccessDenied.

Linked-role CloudTrail actor is arn:aws:sts::000000000000:assumed-role/AWSServiceRoleForApplicationAutoScaling_ECSService/AutoScaling-VerifyServiceLinkedRole, invokedBy ecs.application-autoscaling.amazonaws.com; original-caller forwarded requests instead use each probe role ARN, invokedBy application-autoscaling.amazonaws.com.
observations.denialStateInterpretation: No outer RegisterScalableTarget request was denied, so denialPreservedState is null, not a passing no-mutation claim. The downstream ECS AccessDenied events did not prevent target creation or mutation. Direct ECS controls all used desiredCount 0 where allowed and left the service at zero.
limitations: This capture does not establish behavior for positive min/max bounds, a missing/unusable linked role, nonzero tasks, scaling policy creation, or runtime scaling.

Fixed role policies were created once, then allowed at least 30 seconds propagation before fresh sessions. Direct ECS controls and forwarded CloudTrail errors corroborate effective missing/denied permissions rather than relying only on elapsed time.

CloudTrail collection was eventually consistent and bounded to five pages per event name per poll, initially 180 seconds maximum plus a supplemental 180-second maximum. All 16 probe-role RegisterScalableTarget events and two forwarded calls of each ECS operation per role were captured.
